summary: Green growth is visible, but rye coverage still needs a closer look. Keep thin areas moist without saturating the lawn.

cards.name: New rye lawn
cards.action: Keep the seedbed moist with gentle watering while unsprouted areas continue germinating. Skip runs where soil is already wet. Do not reduce watering across the entire lawn just because a few areas sprouted; keep the old two-hour program off.
cards.amount: Enough to moisten the seedbed without puddles or runoff; sprinkler output has not been measured.
cards.frequency: Check around 7 AM, 11 AM, 2 PM and 5 PM; water only as needed to prevent the seedbed drying, without runoff.
cards.nextCheck: Coverage check due now: send close-ups of one thin and one greener area, and measure the new rye height before deciding on spot repairs, watering reduction or first mowing.
cards.why: First sprouts are confirmed, but an overview cannot reliably separate new rye from older Bermuda. Thin, straw-colored areas alone are not proof that seeding failed.

cards.name: Green hopseed
cards.action: Check moisture inside the original root ball daily. Hand-water slowly when it begins drying, keeping it moist rather than soggy.
cards.amount: Wet the root ball and nearby soil; an exact volume needs a moisture and delivery check.
cards.frequency: Continue daily moisture checks during establishment; watering remains conditional. Do not change the shared valve schedule before checking emitter delivery and soil.
cards.nextCheck: Drip readiness check due: report whether the root ball is moist or drying and identify emitter GPH and count.
cards.why: New shrub roots need reliable moisture. Nursery container size is not a watering dose.

cards.name: Barrel & totem cactus
cards.action: Check soil beneath the gravel beside the root ball. If still moist, skip watering. If it is drying, use the installer’s brief hose watering at a gentle flow, aimed at soil rather than the cactus body. Do not add a drip run as well.
cards.amount: Installer’s starting instruction: about 30 seconds with a hose. Flow rate is unmeasured; use the gentle flow demonstrated rather than assuming every hose setting gives the same amount.
cards.frequency: Check soil before any watering. The brief installer-directed hose routine is provisional, not an indefinite daily watering schedule.
cards.nextCheck: Establishment review due: check whether root-area soil dries between waterings before choosing a longer-term interval. No automatic twice-weekly drip.
cards.why: These were nursery-pot plants. Root condition is unknown, so use the installer’s method with moisture checks rather than applying a blanket bare-root transplant rule.

cards.name: Moroccan mound
cards.action: Keep it on a separate low-water approach from the hopseed. Let soil dry between waterings.
cards.amount: Avoid saturating the root area repeatedly; exact delivery is not yet calibrated.
cards.frequency: Check soil first; no automatic extra hand-watering while wet.
cards.nextCheck: Review soil moisture before connecting it to a frequent shared drip schedule.
cards.why: This is a succulent, not a shrub that should stay steadily moist.

cards.name: Hybrid fan & Mediterranean fan palms
cards.action: Check root-zone moisture before a drip run. Do not increase watering simply because new plants were added.
cards.amount: Recorded baseline: about 24 gallons per palm per run; this has not been validated against root-zone wetting.
cards.frequency: Recorded baseline: about every four days. Skip or adjust when soil is already wet.
cards.nextCheck: Check the root area before the next scheduled run.
cards.why: Emitter flow controls volume, but every plant on a valve shares its watering days.

tasks.title: First rye fertilizer
tasks.instruction: Planned first rye feeding: 1.54 lb total of plain Scotts Starter 24-25-4, with Scotts drop setting 6 subject to the actual bag/model. Apply only once, provided seedlings are established and conditions are suitable. If starter was already applied at seeding, skip this additional feeding.

tasks.title: Lawn recovery check
tasks.instruction: Compare a thin area and a greener area with close-up photos taken without glare. Measure the new rye blades, not taller old grass. Await assessment before adding seed or making a whole-lawn watering change; do not rake through sprouts.
tasks.when: Due now · coverage and height check

tasks.title: New plant drip review
tasks.instruction: Check hopseed root-ball moisture and identify its emitter count and GPH before moving to drip. Do not switch all plants to twice-weekly watering automatically. Assess cacti and Moroccan mound separately; keep cactus drip off if using hand-watering.
tasks.when: Due now · root moisture and emitter check

tasks.title: First rye mowing
tasks.instruction: Wait until the NEW rye reaches about 2¾–3 inches and is rooted enough for mowing. With a rotary mower, use a sharp blade set around 2½ inches. Mow only with dry grass and firm soil, turn gently and avoid scalping thin areas. Do not judge readiness from taller old grass alone.
